questions.question: A man travels some distance at a speed of 12 km/hr and returns at a speed of 9 km/hr. If the total time taken by him is 2 hrs 20 min, the distance is
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Total time taken = 2 hours 20 minutes = 2 + 20/60 = 2 + 1/3 = 7/3 hours.

Shortcut formula for distance when total time for a round trip is known: Distance = (S₁ × S₂) / (S₁ + S₂) × Total Time

Distance = (12 × 9) / (12 + 9) × (7/3)

Distance = (108 / 21) × (7/3) = (36 / 7) × (7/3) = 12 km.

**∴ The correct answer is 12 km.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Speed while going (S₁) = 12 km/hr

Speed while returning (S₂) = 9 km/hr

Total time (T) = 2 hours 20 minutes = 7/3 hours

**Formula Used:**

Time = Distance ÷ Speed

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/b59e46f51d3cc5655a24aac145b38d0d0457db78a7de3f9c56b15b01bea82b09.png] 

**Calculations:**

⇒ Let the distance between the two points be 'd' km.

⇒ Time taken to travel from A to B = d/12 hours

⇒ Time taken to travel from B to A = d/9 hours

⇒ According to the question: d/12 + d/9 = 7/3

⇒ Taking LCM of 12 and 9 (which is 36): (3d + 4d) / 36 = 7/3

⇒ 7d / 36 = 7/3

⇒ d = (7/3) × (36/7)

⇒ d = 12 km

**∴ The correct answer is 12 km.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Average Speed for Same Distance

When a person covers equal distances at speeds x and y, the average speed for the whole journey is (2xy) / (x + y).

Distance Formula (Time Difference)

If the difference in time taken at two different speeds is ΔT, then Distance = [ (S₁ × S₂) / |S₁ − S₂| ] × ΔT.

Unit Conversion

To convert speed from km/hr to m/s, multiply by 5/18. To convert from m/s to km/hr, multiply by 18/5.</p

questions.question: Excluding stoppages, the speed of a bus is 80 kmph and including stoppages, it is 60 kmph. For how many minutes does the bus stop per hour?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**15**__
**__Key Points__**
__

• The speed of the bus **excluding stoppages** is **80 kmph**. This implies that in one hour of continuous running, the bus covers **80 kilometers**.

• The speed of the bus **including stoppages** is **60 kmph**. This means that in one actual hour (including stop time), the bus covers only **60 kilometers**.

• The **reduction in distance** covered in one hour due to stops is: 80 − 60 = **20 km**.

• The **stop time** is equivalent to the time the bus would have taken to cover those **20 km** if it had been running at its non-stop speed of **80 kmph**.

• Using the formula: **Time = Distance ÷ Speed**.

• Stoppage time in hours = 20 ÷ 80 = **1/4 hour**.

• To convert hours into minutes: 1/4 × 60 = **15 minutes**.

• Therefore, the bus stops for **15 minutes** every hour.

**Additional Information__**

• A quick **shortcut formula** for this type of problem is: **Stop time per hour = (Faster Speed − Slower Speed) ÷ Faster Speed**.

• Applying the formula: (80 − 60) ÷ 80 = 20 ÷ 80 = 1/4 hour. Multiply by 60 to get **15 minutes**.

• This logic is based on the fact that the **deficit in distance** is entirely due to the time spent at **stoppages**, during which the bus is not moving at its **constant speed**.

• Understanding the difference between **Average Speed** and **Instantaneous Speed** is crucial in solving **Time, Speed, and Distance** problems.
</ul

questions.question: A and B are 15 kms apart and when travelling towards each other meet after half an hour whereas they meet two and a half hours later if they travel in the same direction. The faster of the two travels at the speed of
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Sum of speeds (opposite direction) = 15 ÷ 0.5 = 30 km/hr

Difference of speeds (same direction) = 15 ÷ 2.5 = 6 km/hr

Speed of faster person = (Sum + Difference) ÷ 2

Faster speed = (30 + 6) ÷ 2 = 36 ÷ 2 = 18 km/hr

**∴ The correct answer is 18 km/hr.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Distance (D) = 15 km

Time for opposite direction (t₁) = 0.5 hr

Time for same direction (t₂) = 2.5 hr

**Formula Used:**

Relative Speed (Opposite) = S₁ + S₂ = Distance ÷ Time₁

Relative Speed (Same) = S₁ − S₂ = Distance ÷ Time₂

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/a42db0ecdf1e9285652026c65dbf4c3debaa6b2d47924063dd5c40f6775bead3.png] 

**Calculations:**

⇒ Let the speed of the faster person be x km/hr and the slower be y km/hr.

⇒ x + y = 15 ÷ 0.5

⇒ x + y = 30 ---- (Eq. 1)

⇒ x − y = 15 ÷ 2.5

⇒ x − y = 6 ---- (Eq. 2)

⇒ Adding (Eq. 1) and (Eq. 2):

⇒ (x + y) + (x − y) = 30 + 6

⇒ 2x = 36

⇒ x = 18 km/hr

⇒ Substituting x in (Eq. 1): 18 + y = 30 → y = 12 km/hr

**∴ The correct answer is 18 km/hr.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Relative Speed Concept

When two bodies move in the same direction, relative speed is the difference (S₁ − S₂). When they move in opposite directions, it is the sum (S₁ + S₂).

Conversion of Units

To convert speed from km/hr to m/s, multiply by 5/18. To convert from m/s to km/hr, multiply by 18/5.

Average Speed

If a person travels equal distances at speeds x and y, then the average speed for the whole journey is (2 × x × y) ÷ (x + y).</p

questions.question: Rubi goes to a multiplex at the speed of 3 km/hr to see a movie and reaches 5 minutes late. If she travels at the speed of 4 Km/hr she reaches 5 minutes early. Then the distance of the multiplex from her starting point is
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Use the direct formula for distance when reaching late and early:

Distance = [ (Product of Speeds) ÷ (Difference of Speeds) ] × Total Time Difference

Time Difference = 5 min late + 5 min early = 10 minutes = 10/60 hours = 1/6 hr

Distance = [ (3 × 4) ÷ (4 − 3) ] × (1/6)

Distance = [ 12 ÷ 1 ] × (1/6) = 12 × (1/6) = 2 km

**∴ The correct answer is 2 km.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Speed 1 (s₁) = 3 km/hr | Speed 2 (s₂) = 4 km/hr

Time 1 = Actual Time + 5 min | Time 2 = Actual Time − 5 min

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/7299649b6f52c16ec79d8497de44999de820b3607f251d7154142cdecc5b0dae.png] 

Since Distance is constant, Speed (s) is inversely proportional to Time (t):

⇒ Ratio of speeds = s₁ : s₂ = 3 : 4

⇒ Ratio of times = t₁ : t₂ = 4 : 3

⇒ Difference in time units = 4 − 3 = 1 unit

⇒ Actual time difference = 5 min late − (−5 min early) = 10 minutes

⇒ 1 unit = 10 minutes = 10/60 hr = 1/6 hr

⇒ Time taken at 3 km/hr (t₁) = 4 units = 4 × (1/6) = 2/3 hr

⇒ Distance = Speed × Time

⇒ Distance = 3 km/hr × (2/3) hr = 2 km

**∴ The correct answer is 2 km.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Time Difference Rule

If both cases are late or both are early, subtract the times. If one is late and one is early, add the times to find the total difference.

Average Speed

When the distance covered is the same for two different speeds x and y, the Average Speed = (2 × x × y) ÷ (x + y).

Speed-Time Relationship

For a fixed distance, speed and time are inversely proportional (s₁/s₂ = t₂/t₁).</p

questions.question: Two donkeys are standing 400 meters apart. First donkey can run at a speed of 3 m/sec and the second can run at 2 m/sec. If two donkeys run towards each other after how much time (in sec) will they bump into each other?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Relative Speed (opposite direction) = Speed 1 + Speed 2

Relative Speed = 3 + 2 = 5 m/sec

Time required = Total Distance ÷ Relative Speed

Time = 400 ÷ 5 = 80 sec

**∴ The correct answer is 80 sec.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Distance (D) = 400 m

Speed of first donkey (s₁) = 3 m/sec

Speed of second donkey (s₂) = 2 m/sec

**Formula Used:**

Time = Distance ÷ Relative Speed

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/98cbf7430078781f4991a1518bc7f2eaffc5fdf8704b3a4e4dae6d672249e15d.png] 

**Calculations:**

⇒ When two objects move towards each other, relative speed is the sum of individual speeds.

⇒ Relative Speed = s₁ + s₂

⇒ Relative Speed = 3 + 2 = 5 m/sec

⇒ Time = Distance ÷ Relative Speed

⇒ Time = 400 ÷ 5

⇒ Time = 80 sec

**∴ The correct answer is 80 sec.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Relative Speed in Same Direction

When two objects move in the same direction, Relative Speed = |Speed₁ − Speed₂|.

Unit Conversion

To convert km/hr to m/sec, multiply the value by 5/18. To convert m/sec to km/hr, multiply by 18/5.

Average Speed

For the same distance covered at two different speeds x and y, the average speed is given by 2xy ÷ (x + y).</p

questions.question: A man starts from his house and travelling at 30 km/h, he reaches his office late by 10 minutes, and travelling at 24 km/h, he reaches his office late by 18 minutes. The distance (in km) from his house to his office is∶
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Use the formula: Distance = [Product of Speeds ÷ Difference of Speeds] × Time Difference

Speed₁ = 30 km/h, Speed₂ = 24 km/h

Time Difference = 18 min − 10 min = 8 min = 8 ÷ 60 hours

Distance = [ (30 × 24) ÷ (30 − 24) ] × (8 ÷ 60)

Distance = [ 720 ÷ 6 ] × (2 ÷ 15) = 120 × (2 ÷ 15) = 8 × 2 = 16 km

**∴ The correct answer is 16 km.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Speed₁ (S₁) = 30 km/h, Arrival = 10 min late

Speed₂ (S₂) = 24 km/h, Arrival = 18 min late

**Formula Used:**

Distance (D) = [ (S₁ × S₂) ÷ |S₁ − S₂| ] × ΔT

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/af575b4b6322aba9f124c1abb20b2a6bf94fc8372e8f4a4f17d8be0aedd0a2c9.png] 

**Calculations:**

⇒ Let the actual time to reach be 'T' minutes.

⇒ Time taken at 30 km/h (T₁) = T + 10 min

⇒ Time taken at 24 km/h (T₂) = T + 18 min

⇒ Time difference (ΔT) = T₂ − T₁ = (T + 18) − (T + 10) = 8 min

⇒ Convert ΔT to hours: ΔT = 8 ÷ 60 = 2 ÷ 15 hours

⇒ Using speed-distance relation: Distance = Speed × Time

⇒ D = [ (30 × 24) ÷ (30 − 24) ] × (2 ÷ 15)

⇒ D = [ 720 ÷ 6 ] × (2 ÷ 15)

⇒ D = 120 × (2 ÷ 15)

⇒ D = 8 × 2 = 16 km

**∴ The correct answer is 16 km.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Speed-Time Relationship

When distance is constant, speed is inversely proportional to time: S₁ × T₁ = S₂ × T₂ or S₁/S₂ = T₂/T₁.

Time Difference Rule

If one speed leads to being 'x' minutes late and another to 'y' minutes late, the time difference ΔT = |x − y|. If one is late and another is early, ΔT = x + y.

Average Speed for Constant Distance

If a person covers the same distance at two different speeds S₁ and S₂, the average speed for the whole journey is 2S₁S₂ ÷ (S₁ + S₂).</p

questions.question: Train A which was travelling at 50 km/h crosses train B travelling in opposite direction in 15 seconds. If the length of train B is three times the length of A and the speed of train B was 58 km/h, then the length of train A(in m) is∶
questions.solution:
__Shortcut Trick__

Relative speed in opposite direction = 50 + 58 = 108 km/h

Relative speed in m/s = 108 × 5/18 = 30 m/s

Total distance (LA + LB) = Speed × Time = 30 × 15 = 450 m

Given LB = 3LA, so total length = LA + 3LA = 4LA

4LA = 450 ⇒ LA = 450 ÷ 4 = 112.5 m

**∴ The correct answer is 112.5 m.**

**__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Speed of Train A (SA) = 50 km/h

Speed of Train B (SB) = 58 km/h

Time to cross each other (t) = 15 seconds

Length of Train B (LB) = 3 × Length of Train A (LA)

**Formula Used:**

Relative Speed (Opposite Direction) = SA + SB

Total Distance = Length of Train A + Length of Train B

Distance = Speed × Time

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/bf1fad83d0bad5455dc1fe94125b463d6954dea1bc670d4be8e00ca608489a17.png] 

**Calculations:**

⇒ Relative speed = 50 + 58 = 108 km/h

⇒ Converting speed to m/s: 108 × (5/18) = 6 × 5 = 30 m/s

⇒ Total distance = (LA + LB)

⇒ LA + 3LA = 30 × 15

⇒ 4LA = 450

⇒ LA = 450 ÷ 4

⇒ LA = 112.5 m

**∴ The correct answer is 112.5 m.**

**__Additional Information__**

Relative Speed Rules

When two objects move in opposite directions, relative speed = S₁ + S₂. When they move in the same direction, relative speed = |S₁ − S₂|.

Unit Conversion

To convert km/h to m/s, multiply by 5/18. To convert m/s to km/h, multiply by 18/5.

Crossing Length

When a train crosses another train, the total distance covered is always the sum of the lengths of both trains, regardless of the direction.</p

questions.question: A takes 2 hours more than B to cover a distance of 40 km. If A doubles his speed, he takes 1(1)/(2) hours more than B to cover 80 km. To cover a distance of 90 km, how much time will B take travelling at his same speed?
questions.solution:
__Shortcut Trick__

For 40 km, Time difference (A − B) = 2 hours.

For 80 km at 2 × Speed A, A's time is the same as for 40 km at Speed A.

New difference for 80 km: Time A (for 40 km) − Time B (for 80 km) = 1.5 hours.

Difference in B's times for 80 km and 40 km = 2 − 1.5 = 0.5 hours.

B covers the extra 40 km in 0.5 hours ⇒ Speed of B = 40 ÷ 0.5 = 80 kmph.

Time for 90 km = 90 ÷ 80 = 1 1/8 hours.

**∴ The correct answer is 1 1/8 hours.**

**__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Distance 1 = 40 km, Distance 2 = 80 km, Time difference 1 = 2 hours, Time difference 2 = 1.5 hours.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/008a409c7f47bb6f046eca5b564aeab7022fd1a41b604aabd25947504805ebe4.png] 

**Calculations:**

Let SA and SB be the speeds of A and B respectively.

⇒ Case 1: 40/SA − 40/SB = 2 ... (i)

⇒ Case 2: 80/(2SA) − 80/SB = 1.5

⇒ 40/SA − 80/SB = 1.5 ... (ii)

⇒ From (i), 40/SA = 40/SB + 2

⇒ Substitute this in (ii): (40/SB + 2) − 80/SB = 1.5

⇒ 2 − 1.5 = 80/SB − 40/SB

⇒ 0.5 = 40/SB

⇒ SB = 40 ÷ 0.5 = 80 kmph

⇒ Time taken by B to cover 90 km = 90 ÷ 80

⇒ Time = 9/8 = 1 1/8 hours.

**∴ The correct answer is 1 1/8 hours.**

**__Additional Information__**

Basic Speed-Distance Formula

Speed = Distance ÷ Time | Distance = Speed × Time | Time = Distance ÷ Speed

Relative Speed

When two objects move in the same direction, relative speed = S₁ − S₂. When they move in opposite directions, relative speed = S₁ + S₂.

Average Speed

For the same distance covered at speeds x and y, Average Speed = (2 × x × y) ÷ (x + y).

Inverse Proportion

For a constant distance, speed is inversely proportional to time (S ∝ 1/T). If speed doubles, time is halved.</p

questions.question: A train travelling at the speed of x km/h crossed a 200 m long platform in 30 seconds and overtook a man walking in the same direction at the speed of 6 km/h in 20 seconds. What is the value of x?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Distance difference = Platform length = 200 m.

This difference arises from the difference in (Effective Speed × Time).

200 = [x × 30 − (x − 6) × 20] × 5/18

200 × 18/5 = 30x − 20x + 120

720 = 10x + 120 ⇒ 10x = 600 ⇒ x = 60

**∴ The correct answer is 60 km/h.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Speed of train = x km/h

Length of platform = 200 m

Time to cross platform = 30 s

Speed of man = 6 km/h (same direction)

Time to overtake man = 20 s

**Formula Used:**

Distance = Speed × Time

Relative speed (same direction) = S₁ − S₂

Conversion: 1 km/h = 5/18 m/s

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/daa1526fd24d924312c5f69f43055a4013d0452be21f03e626d31c6ae239e53a.png] 

**Calculations:**

Let the length of the train be L meters.

For crossing the platform:

⇒ L + 200 = [x × 5/18] × 30

⇒ L + 200 = 25x/3 ... (Eq. 1)

For overtaking the man:

⇒ Relative Speed = (x − 6) × 5/18 m/s

⇒ L = [(x − 6) × 5/18] × 20

⇒ L = 50(x − 6)/9 ... (Eq. 2)

Substitute Eq. 2 into Eq. 1:

⇒ [50(x − 6)/9] + 200 = 25x/3

Multiply the entire equation by 9 to clear denominators:

⇒ 50(x − 6) + 1800 = 75x

⇒ 50x − 300 + 1800 = 75x

⇒ 1500 = 75x − 50x

⇒ 1500 = 25x

⇒ x = 1500 ÷ 25

⇒ x = 60

**∴ The correct answer is 60 km/h.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Relative Speed Concept

When two objects move in the same direction, relative speed is S₁ − S₂. When they move in opposite directions, relative speed is S₁ + S₂.

Train Crossing Objects

To cross a point object (pole/man), distance = length of train. To cross a platform/bridge/tunnel, distance = length of train + length of object.

Unit Conversion

To convert km/h to m/s, multiply by 5/18. To convert m/s to km/h, multiply by 18/5.</p

questions.question: Two runners A and B start running at 12 km/hr and 16 km/hr towards each other. They meet after 1 hour and 30 minutes. How far (in km) were they from each other when they started?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Relative Speed (towards each other) = Speed A + Speed B = 12 + 16 = 28 km/hr.

Time = 1 hour 30 minutes = 1.5 hours.

Initial Distance = Relative Speed × Time.

Distance = 28 × 1.5 = 42 km.

**∴ The correct answer is 42 km.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Speed of runner A (SA) = 12 km/hr

Speed of runner B (SB) = 16 km/hr

Meeting time (T) = 1 hour 30 minutes

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/0d66f3f355590009c64ff7474b4c3142fe008a3fc5a241b1cd6e5b4102740d71.png] 

**Formula:**

Total Distance = (Relative Speed) × Time

**Calculations:**

⇒ Time in hours = 1 + 30/60 = 1.5 hours

⇒ Relative Speed (Opposite Direction) = SA + SB

⇒ Relative Speed = 12 + 16 = 28 km/hr

⇒ Distance = 28 × 1.5

⇒ Distance = 28 × 3/2

⇒ Distance = 14 × 3 = 42 km

**∴ The correct answer is 42 km.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Relative Speed Concept

When two objects move towards each other, relative speed is the sum of their individual speeds (S₁ + S₂). If they move in the same direction, it is the difference (S₁ − S₂).

Distance-Speed-Time Relation

The basic formula is Distance = Speed × Time. To find time, use Time = Distance ÷ Speed.

Unit Conversion

Always ensure units are consistent. To convert minutes to hours, divide by 60. To convert km/hr to m/s, multiply by 5/18.</p
